summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest pressure following her recent bilateral nephrectomy. She was found to be in atrial flutter with a rapid ventricular rate, and imaging revealed new bilateral pleural effusions and possible pericardial effusion. An echocardiogram showed a reduced ejection fraction of 29%, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure, likely exacerbated by tachycardia. She underwent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration, resulting in significant symptom improvement. A transesophageal echocardiogram ruled out intracardiac clots, and successful cardioversion restored sinus rhythm. Her warfarin dose was adjusted due to a subtherapeutic INR on admission, and she was transitioned from atenolol to metoprolol for better rate control. Amlodipine was discontinued due to well-controlled blood pressure. She remained afebrile without diarrhea, and her C. diff treatment was continued. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for cardiology and infectious disease.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other parts of uterus
